trials.label: r1c1
trials.name: reference hedged net
trials.hypothesis: The world-2 reference net, unchanged: the mask is read under 4 layouts (as is, transpose, y-flip, x-flip), and the 4 output maps are re-laid the same way and summed. It is the baseline for the hedge. If this world's action layout is one of those 4, it should score above 0 in training. A 0 here while the 16-layout version succeeds would show a type-minor or combined-symmetry layout.

trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: 16-layout hedge
trials.hypothesis: Covers all 8 grid symmetries (with or without transpose, y-flip, x-flip) times type-major and type-minor action order, on both the mask inputs and the output maps. The re-laid maps are summed. This targets action-index deviations the 4-layout reference misses. It is refuted if this scores 0 in training while the reference scores above 0, or if both stay at 0.

trials.label: r1c3
trials.name: reference with 5x5 head
trials.hypothesis: The reference net with its 3x3 head conv replaced by a 5x5 conv. Each output cell then sees ±2 cells, which hedges anchors other than top-left (centre or bottom-right) and footprints larger or shifted from the description. It is refuted if it does no better than the reference, or scores 0 while the reference scores above 0. The extra FLOPs (r about 1.4) cost about 30% of the samples.

trials.label: r1c4
trials.name: 16-layout + global action bias
trials.hypothesis: The 16-layout hedge plus a full-scale Linear (global features to all n_actions logits), added to every logit. This lets any action index, including one that is really DONE but not last, depend on the global state. It targets a moved DONE index and other global action effects. It is refuted if it matches or trails the plain 16-layout hedge, or if both score 0.

trials.label: r1c5
trials.name: 16-layout + obs symmetric views
trials.hypothesis: The 16-layout hedge, with the obs fed as is, transposed (on square grids), y-flipped and x-flipped, all concatenated before the learned stem. Each action cell then sees the obs at its mirrored or transposed location. This targets an obs grid laid out differently from the mask and action grid. It is refuted if it does no better than the plain 16-layout hedge.

trials.label: r1c6
trials.name: all hedges combined
trials.hypothesis: Combines all four bets: 16 action layouts, symmetric obs views, a 5x5 head conv and a global action bias. If the world has several deviations at once, only a combined hedge can fit it. The cost is r about 1.6, so about 40% fewer samples. It is refuted if it scores 0 while any single-hedge candidate succeeds, which would mean the extra inputs dilute learning.

trials.label: r2c1
trials.name: 24-layout axis permutations
trials.hypothesis: Hedges all 6 orders of the (type, y, x) action axes times 4 flips, adding the type-middle orders (y,t,x) and (x,t,y) that round 1 missed, on both the mask inputs and the output maps. The trunk and recipe are the reference's. Targets an action index with type in the middle. Refuted if training success stays 0.

trials.label: r2c2
trials.name: anchor-hedged footprint pooling
trials.hypothesis: Uses the 16-layout hedge and adds max/min pooling over each footprint and its swap, under all 4 corner anchors, on a learned projection, mixed with the 3x3 head. Landing height is the max over the footprint, which a 3x3 conv learns slowly. This bias failed before only when anchors and footprints were hard-coded, and here they are hedged. Refuted if training success stays 0.

trials.label: r2c3
trials.name: global/row-col context + stem norm
trials.hypothesis: Uses the 16-layout hedge, and each residual block adds a broadcast of global mean/max plus row and column means, so every cell sees the whole grid. A GroupNorm follows the first learned stem conv. Targets non-local dynamics (sliding or support rules) and badly scaled obs channels such as raw heights or step counts. Refuted if training success stays 0.

trials.label: r2c4
trials.name: dilated 3-block trunk, 1 epoch
trials.hypothesis: Uses the 16-layout hedge with three residual 3x3 blocks at dilations 1, 2 and 4, so the receptive field covers the whole grid, and trains with 1 PPO epoch (about 330k steps instead of 240k). Targets dynamics with long-range effects together with slow learning. Unlike earlier single recipe tweaks, it changes the trunk's range too. Refuted if training success stays 0.

trials.label: r2c5
trials.name: attention bridge over cells
trials.hypothesis: Uses the 16-layout hedge and adds one residual self-attention layer over all grid cells, with learned positional embeddings, after the conv trunk. Any cell can then read any other cell, which covers non-dihedral spatial relations between the obs frame and the action frame and long-range dynamics. Earlier transformers were used as heads; here attention only supplements a conv trunk. Refuted if training success stays 0.

trials.label: r2c6
trials.name: combined v2: 24 layouts+pool+context
trials.hypothesis: Combines all 24 axis-order layouts, footprint pooling hedged over anchors and swaps, global/row-col context blocks and the stem GroupNorm. If the world has several deviations at once, only a combined hedge can fit it. At r about 1.45 it gets about 30% fewer samples. Refuted if it scores 0 while a single-change candidate succeeds, which would mean the extra inputs dilute learning.

trials.label: r3c1
trials.name: decoupled scaled critic
trials.hypothesis: Untested deviation: the reward or return scale. The critic gets its own small MLP over detached trunk features plus a cheap 1x1 obs conv. Its gradient is scaled by 0.1 without changing its output. Adam keeps the critic learning at normal speed, but a large value loss can no longer dominate the global gradient-norm clip or distort the shared trunk. Base is the 16-layout hedge. Refuted if training success stays 0.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 2e-3, "n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 2, "ent_coef": 0.002, "gamma": 0.9, "gae_lambda": 0.85}

ORDERS = ("tyx", "txy", "yxt", "xyt")
ADAPT = False
SEP_CRITIC = True
CRIT_SCALE = 0.1
FLATMASK = False
LAYERS = False
STEM = 64
W = 40
HP = 32
LW = 16
VW = 32


def make_layouts():
    return [(o, fy, fx) for o in ORDERS for fy in (False, True) for fx in (False, True)]


def flip_dims(fy, fx):
    d = []
    if fy:
        d.append(2)
    if fx:
        d.append(3)
    return d


def to_grid(m, lay, T, Y, X):
    order, fy, fx = lay
    size = {"t": T, "y": Y, "x": X}
    g = m.reshape(m.shape[0], size[order[0]], size[order[1]], size[order[2]])
    g = g.permute(0, 1 + order.index("t"), 1 + order.index("y"), 1 + order.index("x"))
    d = flip_dims(fy, fx)
    if d:
        g = g.flip(d)
    return g


def from_grid(g, lay):
    order, fy, fx = lay
    d = flip_dims(fy, fx)
    if d:
        g = g.flip(d)
    g = g.permute(0, 1 + "tyx".index(order[0]), 1 + "tyx".index(order[1]), 1 + "tyx".index(order[2]))
    return g.reshape(g.shape[0], -1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Y, self.X, self.T, self.Z = spec.Y, spec.X, spec.n_types, spec.Z
        self.C = spec.in_channels
        self.n_place = spec.n_place
        self.n_extra = spec.n_actions - spec.n_place
        self.ok = spec.n_place == self.T * self.Y * self.X
        self.lays = make_layouts()
        oc = self.C
        if ADAPT:
            self.adapt = nn.Conv2d(self.C, 2 * self.C, 1, groups=self.C)
            oc = 2 * self.C
        cin = oc + 2
        if self.ok:
            cin += self.T * len(self.lays)
        else:
            self.mask_emb = nn.Linear(spec.n_actions, 4 * self.Y * self.X)
            cin += 4
        self.stem1 = nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1)
        self.stem2 = nn.Conv2d(STEM, W, 1)
        self.use_layers = LAYERS and self.C == 4 * self.Z + 3 and self.Z >= 2
        if self.use_layers:
            self.l1 = nn.Conv2d(14, LW, 1)
            self.l2 = nn.Conv2d(LW, LW, 3, padding=1)
            self.l3 = nn.Conv2d(2 * LW, W, 1)
        self.r1 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.r2 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.hconv = nn.Conv2d(W, HP, 3, padding=1)
        self.hskip = nn.Conv2d(W, HP, 1)
        if self.ok:
            self.outs = nn.Conv2d(HP, self.T * len(self.lays), 1)
        else:
            self.red = nn.Conv2d(HP, 8, 1)
            self.dense = nn.Linear(8 * self.Y * self.X, spec.n_place)
        gin = 2 * W
        if FLATMASK:
            self.mflat = nn.Linear(spec.n_actions, 64)
            gin += 64
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(gin, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, self.n_extra)
        if FLATMASK:
            self.gbias = nn.Linear(64, spec.n_actions)
        if SEP_CRITIC:
            self.vstem = nn.Conv2d(cin, VW, 1)
            self.vnet = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W + 2 * VW, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, 1))
        else:
            self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def layer_branch(self, obs, yy, xx):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        Z, Y, X = self.Z, self.Y, self.X
        ob = obs[:, 0:Z]
        tg = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        ms = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        ex = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        obd = F.pad(ob[:, :Z - 1], (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))
        tgd = F.pad(tg[:, :Z - 1], (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))
        obu = F.pad(ob[:, 1:], (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))
        tgu = F.pad(tg[:, 1:], (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))
        zp = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        per = torch.stack([ob, tg, ms, ex, obd, tgd, obu, tgu, zp], dim=2)
        sh = torch.cat([obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3], yy, xx], dim=1).unsqueeze(1).expand(B, Z, 5, Y, X)
        t = torch.cat([per, sh], dim=2).reshape(B * Z, 14, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.l1(t))
        h = F.relu(h + self.l2(h))
        h = h.reshape(B, Z, LW, Y, X)
        agg = torch.cat([h.amax(1), h.mean(1)], dim=1)
        return self.l3(agg)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        Y, X, T = self.Y, self.X, self.T
        yy = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, Y, 1).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        xx = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, X).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        o = obs
        if ADAPT:
            a = self.adapt(obs)
            o = a / (1.0 + a.abs())
        ins = [o, yy, xx]
        mf = mask.to(obs.dtype)
        if self.ok:
            mp = mf[:, :self.n_place]
            for lay in self.lays:
                ins.append(to_grid(mp, lay, T, Y, X))
        else:
            ins.append(self.mask_emb(mf).view(B, 4, Y, X))
        inp = torch.cat(ins, dim=1)
        x = F.relu(self.stem2(F.relu(self.stem1(inp))))
        if self.use_layers:
            x = F.relu(x + self.layer_branch(obs, yy, xx))
        x = F.relu(x + self.r1(x))
        f = F.relu(x + self.r2(x))
        h = F.relu(self.hconv(f) + self.hskip(f))
        if self.ok:
            maps = self.outs(h)
            place = None
            for k, lay in enumerate(self.lays):
                pk = from_grid(maps[:, k * T:(k + 1) * T], lay)
                place = pk if place is None else place + pk
        else:
            place = self.dense(F.relu(self.red(h)).flatten(1))
        fm = f.mean((2, 3))
        fx = f.amax((2, 3))
        gl = [fm, fx]
        if FLATMASK:
            gl.append(F.relu(self.mflat(mf)))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat(gl, dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        if FLATMASK:
            logits = logits + self.gbias(g)
        if SEP_CRITIC:
            vs = F.relu(self.vstem(inp))
            vf = torch.cat([fm.detach(), fx.detach(), vs.mean((2, 3)), vs.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
            v = self.vnet(vf).squeeze(1)
            v = CRIT_SCALE * v + (1.0 - CRIT_SCALE) * v.detach()
        else:
            v = self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)
        return logits, v


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.hypothesis: Untested deviation: obs values with an unexpected scale, such as raw heights, raw step counts or 0/255 cells. Large inputs saturate logits at once and stop exploration.     order, fy, fx = lay
    size = {"t": T, "y": Y, "x": X}
    g = m.reshape(m.shape[0], size[order[0]], size[order[1]], size[order[2]])
    g = g.permute(0, 1 + order.index("t"), 1 + order.index("y"), 1 + order.index("x"))
    d = flip_dims(fy, fx)
    if d:
        g = g.flip(d)
    return g


def from_grid(g, lay):
    order, fy, fx = lay
    d = flip_dims(fy, fx)
    if d:
        g = g.flip(d)
    g = g.permute(0, 1 + "tyx".index(order[0]), 1 + "tyx".index(order[1]), 1 + "tyx".index(order[2]))
    return g.reshape(g.shape[0], -1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Y, self.X, self.T, self.Z = spec.Y, spec.X, spec.n_types, spec.Z
        self.C = spec.in_channels
        self.n_place = spec.n_place
        self.n_extra = spec.n_actions - spec.n_place
        self.ok = spec.n_place == self.T * self.Y * self.X
        self.lays = make_layouts()
        oc = self.C
        if ADAPT:
            self.adapt = nn.Conv2d(self.C, 2 * self.C, 1, groups=self.C)
            oc = 2 * self.C
        cin = oc + 2
        if self.ok:
            cin += self.T * len(self.lays)
        else:
            self.mask_emb = nn.Linear(spec.n_actions, 4 * self.Y * self.X)
            cin += 4
        self.stem1 = nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1)
        self.stem2 = nn.Conv2d(STEM, W, 1)
        self.use_layers = LAYERS and self.C == 4 * self.Z + 3 and self.Z >= 2
        if self.use_layers:
            self.l1 = nn.Conv2d(14, LW, 1)
            self.l2 = nn.Conv2d(LW, LW, 3, padding=1)
            self.l3 = nn.Conv2d(2 * LW, W, 1)
        self.r1 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.r2 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.hconv = nn.Conv2d(W, HP, 3, padding=1)
        self.hskip = nn.Conv2d(W, HP, 1)
        if self.ok:
            self.outs = nn.Conv2d(HP, self.T * len(self.lays), 1)
        else:
            self.red = nn.Conv2d(HP, 8, 1)
            self.dense = nn.Linear(8 * self.Y * self.X, spec.n_place)
        gin = 2 * W
        if FLATMASK:
            self.mflat = nn.Linear(spec.n_actions, 64)
            gin += 64
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(gin, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, self.n_extra)
        if FLATMASK:
            self.gbias = nn.Linear(64, spec.n_actions)
        if SEP_CRITIC:
            self.vstem = nn.Conv2d(cin, VW, 1)
            self.vnet = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W + 2 * VW, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, 1))
        else:
            self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def layer_branch(self, obs, yy, xx):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        Z, Y, X = self.Z, self.Y, self.X
        ob = obs[:, 0:Z]
        tg = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        ms = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        ex = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        obd = F.pad(ob[:, :Z - 1], (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))
        tgd = F.pad(tg[:, :Z - 1], (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))
        obu = F.pad(ob[:, 1:], (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))
        tgu = F.pad(tg[:, 1:], (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))
        zp = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        per = torch.stack([ob, tg, ms, ex, obd, tgd, obu, tgu, zp], dim=2)
        sh = torch.cat([obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3], yy, xx], dim=1).unsqueeze(1).expand(B, Z, 5, Y, X)
        t = torch.cat([per, sh], dim=2).reshape(B * Z, 14, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.l1(t))
        h = F.relu(h + self.l2(h))
        h = h.reshape(B, Z, LW, Y, X)
        agg = torch.cat([h.amax(1), h.mean(1)], dim=1)
        return self.l3(agg)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        Y, X, T = self.Y, self.X, self.T
        yy = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, Y, 1).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        xx = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, X).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        o = obs
        if ADAPT:
            a = self.adapt(obs)
            o = a / (1.0 + a.abs())
        ins = [o, yy, xx]
        mf = mask.to(obs.dtype)
        if self.ok:
            mp = mf[:, :self.n_place]
            for lay in self.lays:
                ins.append(to_grid(mp, lay, T, Y, X))
        else:
            ins.append(self.mask_emb(mf).view(B, 4, Y, X))
        inp = torch.cat(ins, dim=1)
        x = F.relu(self.stem2(F.relu(self.stem1(inp))))
        if self.use_layers:
            x = F.relu(x + self.layer_branch(obs, yy, xx))
        x = F.relu(x + self.r1(x))
        f = F.relu(x + self.r2(x))
        h = F.relu(self.hconv(f) + self.hskip(f))
        if self.ok:
            maps = self.outs(h)
            place = None
            for k, lay in enumerate(self.lays):
                pk = from_grid(maps[:, k * T:(k + 1) * T], lay)
                place = pk if place is None else place + pk
        else:
            place = self.dense(F.relu(self.red(h)).flatten(1))
        fm = f.mean((2, 3))
        fx = f.amax((2, 3))
        gl = [fm, fx]
        if FLATMASK:
            gl.append(F.relu(self.mflat(mf)))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat(gl, dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        if FLATMASK:
            logits = logits + self.gbias(g)
        if SEP_CRITIC:
            vs = F.relu(self.vstem(inp))
            vf = torch.cat([fm.detach(), fx.detach(), vs.mean((2, 3)), vs.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
            v = self.vnet(vf).squeeze(1)
            v = CRIT_SCALE * v + (1.0 - CRIT_SCALE) * v.detach()
        else:
            v = self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)
        return logits, v


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r4c1
trials.name: mixer trunk + dense head
trials.hypothesis: Each of the 16-layout net's residual blocks gets a full-scale learned token-mixing Linear (YX to YX, per channel), and a dense placement head is added to the conv maps. Any cell can then read any cell through a learned permutation. This targets an obs grid permuted against the action grid in a non-dihedral way, which conv or attention bridges miss. Refuted if training success stays 0.

trials.label: r4c2
trials.name: learned obs spatial remap
trials.hypothesis: Before the stem, a full-scale learned Linear (YX to YX), shared across channels, remaps the obs grid. Its output is concatenated with the raw obs. The 16-layout mask hedge is kept. This targets obs cells stored in a fixed order unrelated to the mask and action grid, such as a scrambled or non-dihedral flattening, which the earlier transpose and flip obs views cannot fit. Refuted if training success stays 0.

trials.label: r4c3
trials.name: DONE-first shifted layouts
trials.hypothesis: Adds a second set of the 16 layouts that reads placements from mask[1:] and writes them to logits[1:], plus its own DONE logit at index 0, summed with the usual set. Every earlier hedge assumed placements start at index 0. If DONE comes first, all placement indices are offset by one, and types and rows wrap wrongly. Refuted if training success stays 0.

trials.label: r4c4
trials.name: combined v4: remap+mixer+dense+shift
trials.hypothesis: Combines this round's untested hedges: the learned obs spatial remap, token-mixing blocks, the dense placement head, and DONE-first shifted layouts on top of the 16 layouts. This covers stacked deviations, for example an index offset plus a scrambled obs grid. r is about 1.4, so it gets fewer samples. Refuted if it stays 0. If a single-change candidate succeeds while this fails, the extra inputs dilute learning.

trials.label: r4c5
trials.name: combined v4, long-horizon 1-epoch
trials.hypothesis: Uses the combined v4 network with a recipe never paired with these hedges: 1 PPO epoch (about 300k steps), rollout 32, gamma 0.99, lambda 0.95, entropy 0.01. If the exact-build bonus is the main signal, or random early play collapses to an early DONE, longer credit assignment, more exploration and more samples could escape zero. Refuted if this stays at 0 while plain combined v4 also stays at 0.

trials.label: r4c6
trials.name: v4 with 24 orders, high entropy
trials.hypothesis: Uses the combined v4 network with all 6 axis orders (24 layouts per shift, so 48 in total), entropy 0.02, gamma 0.97 and rollout 32 at 2 epochs. This covers a type-middle action order with a DONE-first offset, which no earlier trial combined, and the higher entropy resists an early-DONE collapse. Refuted if training success stays 0.

analyses.1: There are no results yet. Earlier searches found that 6 of 7 worlds scored exactly 0 for every trial. The only success came from a net that read the mask under several assumed action layouts and summed matching output maps. That suggests the usual deviation is in how action indices map to the grid, not in the recipe. Nothing in this world is ruled out yet. Most other deviations need no special hedge. Permuted obs channels are already absorbed by the learned 1x1 stem, and a different height limit or dynamics shows up in the legality mask, which every candidate reads. So this round tests five layout bets: (1) the reference net unchanged; (2) a 16-layout hedge covering 8 grid symmetries times type-major or type-minor order; (3) a 5x5 head conv for footprint and anchor shifts; (4) the 16-layout hedge plus a learned dense action bias from global features, in case DONE or other actions sit at unexpected indices; (5) the 16-layout hedge plus symmetric views of the obs, in case the obs is transposed or flipped relative to the mask. The sixth candidate (6) combines all of these. All use the reference recipe.
analyses.2: Every round-1 trial scored 0, in dev and in training. Working back from the parameter counts: r1c1 has 53,130 parameters, which gives cin=45, so in_channels=27, Z=6 and T=4. The extra layer in r1c4 adds 16,705 = 65*257, so n_actions=257. So n_place=256=T*Y*X, DONE comes last, and the grid is square. That rules out a different action count or grid size, which means the dense fallback head never ran. Round 1 also covered, and got 0 from: all 8 grid symmetries between obs and action index (the 16-layout re-laying covers them), type-major and type-minor order, a moved DONE via the global bias, and anchor shifts of ±2. Untested: type-middle action orders, dynamics that need footprint-max or longer-range reasoning, a badly scaled obs, and learning speed. This round tests these, one at a time and combined.
analyses.3: All 12 trials scored 0 on dev and in training. The parameter counts fit the spec as described: r1c1's 53,130 parameters need in_channels=27 (Z=6) and n_types=4, and the attention parameters in r2c5 need Y*X=64 with exactly one DONE. So the grid size, action count and DONE count look normal, and the deviation is in what things mean. Ruled out as the only problem: the 24 axis-order and flip action layouts, obs flips and transposes, footprints and anchors within ±2 cells, a moved DONE or global per-action effects, long-range context, and footprint pooling. Channel permutations cannot be the cause, because the 1x1 stem learns any channel order. Still untested: badly scaled obs values, value-loss or reward-scale problems that drown the policy gradient under the global clip, an action order that is not geometric, and vertical dynamics. This round makes one change per bet on top of the 16-layout hedge, plus one combined candidate.
analyses.4:
All 18 trials scored exactly 0, in training and on dev, so the deviation is still unfound. The results rule out several causes:
- The action index is not one of the 24 axis orders × 4 flips, read the type-major way or the type-minor way.
- The 3x3 and 5x5 heads did not help, so anchors shifted by up to 2 cells are not the cause.
- Mirrored or transposed obs views did not help.
- A global action bias and flat-mask global logits did not help.
- Reward and obs scale hedges did not help.
- Context blocks, attention, dilated trunks and a per-layer 2.5D branch also stayed at 0.
- 1 PPO epoch did not help.

Three ideas are still untested:
1. A non-dihedral spatial mismatch between the obs and the action grid. I test it with full-scale learned YX→YX token mixing on the obs and in the trunk, plus a dense placement head.
2. Placements offset by one index because DONE comes first, which would also shift the mask. I test a shifted layout set with its own DONE logit at index 0.
3. These hedges combined with a longer-horizon, more-exploratory, more-sample recipe.

This is the last round, so I spread the bets rather than refining.
